challenges.name: heap-lifetimes-quiz
challenges.title: Who owns this memory?
challenges.description: Read each snippet the way C runs it: which pointers share one buffer, which functions leak or leave a dangling pointer, and what free really does.

questions.explanation: names[i] = buf stores the ADDRESS of the one array buf, not its characters. All three entries hold the same address, and printf reads the array as it is at the end of the loop, so it prints the last name three times. Nothing here is undefined: buf is still alive. To keep three names you need three copies, for example names[i] = strdup(buf) (and a free for each later).

A allocates strlen(s) + 1 bytes (room for the '\0'), checks for NULL and hands ownership to the caller: correct. B returns the address of a local array whose lifetime ends at the return: the pointer dangles (gcc warns -Wreturn-local-addr). C makes the new copy first, frees the old string it owns, then stores the new one: correct, and on failure the list is unchanged. D overwrites list[i] without freeing the old string, so that block can never be freed again: a leak (LeakSanitizer reports it), and it also ignores a NULL result.

options.text: C - replace_name with strdup, free, store
D - replace_name that only assigns strdup(s)

questions.explanation: a and b are two copies of the same address. free(a) releases the block; a = NULL changes only the variable a, not b, which still holds the old address. free(b) frees the same block a second time: a double free, which is undefined behaviour (ASan reports attempting double-free, gcc warns -Wuse-after-free). Setting a pointer to NULL protects only that one pointer, which is why a block should have exactly one owner that frees it.

options.text: Nothing bad: after a = NULL the second free is a no-op
Double free, undefined behaviour: b still holds the freed address
free(b) frees a separate copy made by b = a
It does not compile: b is a dangling pointer

challenges.name: fix-recent-scans-list
challenges.title: Fix the scanner's recent scans list
challenges.description: The handheld scanner SCN-07 keeps the last few product names in a bounded "recent scans" list: when it is full, the oldest name is dropped. Every entry on the screen shows the LAST scanned name, and after a shift the scanner has leaked memory. Fix recent_add() so it stores an owned copy of each name and frees the entry it drops, and recent_free() so it frees every entry. Allocate only with xmalloc/xstrdup/xfree: the test runner counts live allocations and reports double frees.
